text: Enable screen reader, ensure all main headings and buttons are properly announced
Press Tab to navigate between elements, verify logical focus order sequence
Test button contrast in high-contrast mode: all labels readable, no hidden elements
Check presence and correctness of aria-label for icons, sliders, custom input components
Enable high-contrast and light theme — ensure page adapts without losing interface meaning
Use keyboard only for form interaction: all fields, checkboxes, dropdowns must be accessible
Test appearance and automatic announcement of notifications through screen reader
Verify that images always have alt-text specified, fallback message shown when missing
Play video with subtitles, ensure they are accessible to screen reader
Test autofocus: on validation error field receives focus, screen reader announces error
Verify that tooltips and helper text are accessible via keyboard and screen reader
Ensure unique IDs for roles and ARIA attributes on all interactive elements
Change interface language, verify correct reading of text and errors by screen reader
Ensure all modal dialogs have proper ARIA roles and don't trap focus outside modal
In high-contrast mode check visibility of disabled, hover, selected menu elements
Run Lighthouse/axe audit: all critical accessibility errors must be resolved
Auto-close toast notifications only after being announced by screen reader
Use skip-link for quick navigation to main content via keyboard
Verify that when using ARIA live region, event notifications are announced immediately
Organize content in logical structure: headings, lists, sections — screen reader support
Ensure focus ring support for all elements when navigating with Tab
Enter invalid data in form, ensure error description is announced
Test toggle/switch functionality with current state announcement via screen reader
Verify interactive elements are accessible for control without mouse (Tab/Enter only)
Test on mobile screen readers (TalkBack/VoiceOver), all UI elements accessible for announcement
Test mobile screen reader (TalkBack on Android): tab panel names announced correctly, no errors
On iOS VoiceOver check accessibility of control buttons in bottom navigation
On Android in high contrast mode ensure all icons and labels remain visible
Test accessibility for gestures: swipes, long tap, double-tap accessible to users with motor impairments
Open mobile version: check automatic font adaptation for low-vision users
Simulate disabled sound/vibration: verify notifications via screen reader remain accessible
When internet connection is lost, all accessibility hints and statuses in app must remain accessible
In edge case of auto-focusing input on mobile — verify screen reader announces input
When main styles fail to load (network error) fallback page accessibility is preserved
Test absence of keyboard trap: always have way to exit any modal dialog using Esc/Tab
Enable airplane mode, ensure all main ARIA live notifications continue working on local events
Affect interface scaling through Windows/Mac system settings — ensure all elements remain accessible to screen reader
Simulate bug: incorrect tabindex order causes focus loss — restore validation of blind spots in navigation
When image/icon render fails, fallback question mark text/alt must be announced on mobile screen reader
Accessibility bug: error in aria-describedby causes error text to be ignored — validate nested descriptions
In mobile browser verify that in landscape orientation UI controls accessible only via swipe/focus (no mouse)
Disable screen reader during login form; ensure login intent is explicitly written and accessible
Edge: on Android navigate via external bluetooth keyboard — focus must work through Tab and arrows without loss
Verify that special ARIA hints and patterns injected via external plugins maintain valid accessibility structure
On ultra-wide screens (>2000px) verify all popups and navigation fully readable via screen reader
Enable Braille display and screen reader, ensure all text elements output correctly (no special characters)
On Samsung Internet verify correct ARIA text announcement and TabOrder functionality with Samsung Voice Assistant
Test scenario of connecting third-party accessibility Chrome/Firefox extension: custom reader displays only accessible UI elements
Reproduce bug with disabled JS: control elements must remain accessible to screen reader and Braille
Test that browser zoom (>200%) doesn't cause label overlap and accessibility loss on Braille display
Enable custom high-contrast extension, ensure text and background colors don't conflict with app theme scheme
Edge bug: after drag'n'drop on touch device focus doesn't return to active element — check focus return and Braille announcement
Embed custom ARIA roles via extension, ensure no conflicts with native roles (double role bug)
In Samsung Internet browser test fallback live element updates (if built-in live region not supported)
Remove/add DOM element with active screen reader — verify Braille and Voice are synchronized
Simulate massive dynamic UI changes (carousel, modal overlays) — ensure all screen reader and Braille notifications arrive sequentially, none lost
Test support for aria-busy, aria-details and other edge attributes in modern screen readers, Braille, extensions
Reproduce negative situation when aria-label is empty/missing: screen reader reports inaccessibility, but Braille screen doesn't
Test custom shortcuts for accessibility users (e.g., go to search), ensure they appear accessibly and don't conflict with Braille device
